ghs.en: She came running over to me,
ghs.assessment: The source uses present narration and forms a complete action. 'Came running' shifts to past and leaves the line hanging on a comma.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She comes running over.'

highlights.text: She came running over to me,

rows.jp: お風呂にするそれともご飯、とでも言いそうな勢いと態度だ。
rows.en: She came at me with all the energy of someone about to ask, “Bath or dinner?”

ghs.en: As if wanting to ask me if I would prefer a bath, or dinner, or perhaps...

rows.jp: 「風呂に入りながらご飯を食べゆ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "I'll be taking a bath while I have dinner."
ghs.assessment: 食べゆ is a deliberate babyish slip from 食べる. The English renders an ordinary grammatical 'have dinner' and removes the malformed comic ending.
ghs.remedy: Preserve a controlled childish slip in the final verb.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I'll be taking a bath while I have dinner."

ghs.assessment: そりゃ来るわよ emphatically says 'Of course I came.' 'Seems like I did' turns certainty into a tentative inference.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Of course I came.'

highlights.text: Touko: "Seems like I did, yes!"

ghs.assessment: 荷物 is her luggage or belongings for the move. 'Bags' narrows it to specific containers.
ghs.remedy: Use '...Where is your luggage?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "...the bags?"

rows.en: “So come home with me after school?”

ghs.en: Touko: "So, shall we go home together?"

ghs.assessment: へーい is the narrator's casual acknowledgment, 'Okay.' 'Let's' instead proposes a joint action and leaves the verb omitted.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Okaaay.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Lee-et's."

rows.en: Call it a sort of weariness.

rows.jp: できちゃった結婚を突きつけられた遊び足りない遊び人２２歳ってこんな気持ちなのかな。
rows.en: Was this how a twenty-two-year-old playboy felt when a shotgun wedding caught him with his wild oats only half sown?

ghs.en: The same feelings of a 22 year old playboy that hasn't played enough and is now forced into a wedding due to an unplanned pregnancy.

rows.jp: 「荷物、なに持って行こうかなーって思っていろいろ探したの」
rows.en: “I was looking through everything, wondering what I should bring.”

ghs.en: Touko: "For the baggages, I was wondering, oh what should I bring with, so I went searching all over."
ghs.assessment: 'Baggage' is uncountable in this sense, 'bring with' lacks an object, and the nested 'I was wondering, oh' is not grammatical reported thought.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I looked through all kinds of things, wondering what luggage I should bring.'

highlights.text: Touko: "For the baggages, I was wondering, oh what should I bring with, so I went searching all over."

rows.jp: 「そしたら古い写真が出てきたのよ？」
rows.en: “And guess what I found? Some old photos.”

ghs.en: Touko: "And guess whose old photos turned up?"
ghs.assessment: Guess whose adds an ownership hook, but the photos are hers and the conversational reveal supports it. No wrong-subject finding remains.
ghs.remedy: Use a direct reveal without unnecessary ownership prompting.

highlights.text: Touko: "And guess whose old photos turned up?"

ghs.assessment: The archaic とな is a quotative reaction, 'Old photos, you say.' 'Old pictures aren't they' forms an unrelated tag question.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Oh? Old photographs, you say.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Huh, old pictures aren't they."

rows.jp: 「古い写真なら、俺もいっぱい持ってる」
rows.en: “I have plenty of old photos myself.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I have plenty of old photos, as well."

rows.jp: 「ほんと？　とっておいてくれたんだ」
古い（発禁ヘア）写真（集）なら、俺もいっぱい持ってる。
rows.en: I had plenty of old (banned-for-hair) photo (books), too.

ghs.en: I have plenty of old (illegally non-censored) photo(book)s, as well.
I did not tell a lie.

rows.jp: 「捨てなくてよかった……壁に貼ろうと思うの」
rows.en: “I’m so glad I didn’t throw them away... I think I’ll put them on the walls.”

ghs.en: Touko: "So glad I didn't throw them away... I'm thinking of sticking them to a wall."

rows.jp: 「壁が埋まっちゃうくらいあったわよ」
rows.en: “There were enough to cover them completely.”

ghs.en: Touko: "Until the wall is all buried in them!"

rows.en: I made a show of surprise.

ghs.en: She linked her arm with mine.

rows.jp: くそう、やっぱりこの女は……。
rows.en: Damn it. This woman really was...

ghs.en: Dammit, I knew it, this female...
ghs.assessment: This female is harsher and more dehumanizing, but この女 is already disparaging this woman. Only register is escalated.
ghs.remedy: Use this woman in the intended disparaging voice.

highlights.text: Dammit, I knew it, this female...

rows.jp: 俺は道具袋からアイテムを取り出す。
rows.en: I pulled an item from my tool bag.

ghs.en:
I extract an [ITEM] from the tools bag.
* Tools bag = Taichian promotional item, called the Taichi
Bag. It comes in the shape of a canvas back-pack.
Within, many secret implements are found.
ghs.assessment: The source only says the narrator takes an item from his tool bag. The appended multi-line explanation invents a promotional Taichi Bag and its physical design and contents.
ghs.remedy: Use only 'I take an item from my tool bag.'

highlights.text:
I extract an [ITEM] from the tools bag.
* Tools bag = Taichian promotional item, called the Taichi
Bag. It comes in the shape of a canvas back-pack.
Within, many secret implements are found.

rows.jp: ※道具袋＝太一グッズ。太一袋と呼ばれる。キャンバス地の背負い袋である。秘密道具がたくさん入っている。
rows.en: *Tool bag = Taichi gear. Known as the Taichi Bag. A canvas backpack stuffed with secret gadgets.

rows.jp: それをすかさず「装備」した！

ghs.en: And then I unhesitatingly Equipped it!

ghs.assessment: The standard English compound is 'armband,' not the separated 'arm band' in this sense.
ghs.remedy: Use 'An armband?'

highlights.text: Touko: "An arm band?"

rows.en: The young lady squinted at it.

ghs.en: The young lady looks quite closely.

ghs.assessment: 変換する describes Tōko mentally converting or deciphering the obscured text. 'So finally reads Tōko' uses broken inversion and merely reports reading.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Tōko deciphers it.'

highlights.text: So finally reads Touko.

rows.jp: 「そうだ。俺はバカップルが及ぼす環境への重大な影響を重く見て、毅然とした態度でその規制ならびに抑制に努める立場なのだ」
rows.en: “Exactly. In view of the grave environmental harm caused by lovey-dovey couples, I take the principled position that they must be regulated and suppressed.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Indeed. I have gravely seen the enormity of the impact of Syrupples on the environment, and with manners most firm, I now strive for the position to regulate and furthermore curb said impact."
ghs.assessment: The mock-policy statement says he takes the environmental harm seriously and therefore stands firm in working to regulate and restrain such couples. The English's 'strive for the position' makes the office itself his goal and is syntactically unstable.
ghs.remedy: Use a grammatical mock-policy declaration preserving impact, firm stance, regulation, and restraint.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Indeed. I have gravely seen the enormity of the impact of Syrupples on the environment, and with manners most firm, I now strive for the position to regulate and furthermore curb said impact."

ghs.assessment: 腕組みやめ is a clipped command to stop linking arms. 'Cease this arm linking' uses a non-idiomatic action noun.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Stop linking arms with me.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Cease this arm linking!"

rows.jp: 「い、いつものことながら……なに言ってるのかわからないんだけど」
rows.en: “A-as always... I have no idea what you’re talking about.”

ghs.en: Touko: "It-, it's always like this I know but... what are you even saying, I don't understand."
ghs.assessment: The source is a coherent hesitant complaint. 'It's always like this I know but' and 'what are you even saying, I don't understand' repeat and splice the clauses.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I-it's the same as always... I have no idea what you're talking about.'

highlights.text: Touko: "It-, it's always like this I know but... what are you even saying, I don't understand."

rows.jp: 「人前での没頭的な愛情表現は慎むべし」
rows.en: “No self-absorbed displays of affection in front of other people.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "One ought to be most discreet in immersive displays of affections in front of people."
ghs.assessment: 没頭的な愛情表現 means absorbed or uninhibited displays of affection. 'Immersive displays of affections' uses the wrong collocation and incorrectly pluralizes the mass noun.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Refrain from uninhibited displays of affection in public.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "One ought to be most discreet in immersive displays of affections in front of people."

ghs.assessment: The speaker says there are no people anymore. 'People, but there's no more' is a fragment and uses singular agreement with the plural noun.
ghs.remedy: Use 'But there aren't any people anymore...'

highlights.text: Touko: "People, but there's no more..."

ghs.assessment: 不満げ describes dissatisfaction or displeasure. 'Frustrated' instead attributes thwarted effort.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She looks dissatisfied.'

highlights.text: Appears to be frustrated.

rows.jp: 「桐原、おまえが反転型の勝ち気娘なのはいい」
rows.en: “Kirihara, being a reverse-polarity spitfire is all well and good.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Kirihara, you are the reversible model of overcompetitive girl, and this is fine."
ghs.assessment: 反転型の勝ち気娘 is a reversed or inverted strong-willed-girl type in the narrator's character-archetype framing. 'Reversible model of overcompetitive girl' suggests a mechanism and changes 勝ち気 from spirited to excessive competition.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Kirihara, being an inverted strong-willed-girl type is fine.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Kirihara, you are the reversible model of overcompetitive girl, and this is fine."

rows.jp: 「けどちょっと甘くしたらベタってしすぎるよ！　水気が多すぎだよ！　もっと徹底して勝ち気っぽく行こうよ！　照れる時は厳選。その方が萌え……桐原のためなんだ」
rows.en: “But sweeten you even a little and you turn to syrup! You’re way too runny! Commit to the spitfire act! Ration the blushing. It makes you much more adora—this is for your own good.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But if you get this sweet, you'll also be far too hackneyed! There's too much dampness! Let's be more consistently unyielding! Select carefully when to show shyness. Someone like that is moe... be that, Kirihara!
ghs.assessment: ベタベタ means overly clingy or syrupy, not hackneyed, and the extended character-direction monologue culminates in a lie that this is for Kirihara's sake. The English becomes incoherent at 'Someone like that is moe... be that,' omits that pivot, and lacks a closing quotation mark.
ghs.remedy: Rebuild the monologue around excessive sweetness, emotional dampness, consistent assertiveness, selective embarrassment, and the final claim that it is for Kirihara's sake; close the quotation.

highlights.text: Taichi: "But if you get this sweet, you'll also be far too hackneyed! There's too much dampness! Let's be more consistently unyielding! Select carefully when to show shyness. Someone like that is moe... be that, Kirihara!

rows.jp: 「おまえは宝石のような女だ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "You are a woman so like a precious gem."

rows.en: I laid a hand on her shoulder and spoke.

ghs.en: I say that as I put a hand on her shoulder.

rows.jp: 「その輝きはダイヤモンドにまさる……だが悲しいかな、ダイヤは炭素なので火にくべたら燃えてしまうんだ。ガッデム」
rows.en: “Your brilliance outshines any diamond... But alas, diamonds are carbon. Throw one in a fire and it burns. Goddamn.”

rows.jp: 「生涯かけてたくわえた富をダイヤで保存することの愚かしさがよくわかるというものさ」
rows.en: “So much for the wisdom of storing a lifetime’s wealth in diamonds.”

rows.jp: 髪の束をつまんで鼻先に当て、香りを楽しむ。
rows.en: I lifted a lock of her hair to my nose and savored its fragrance.

ghs.en: I pinch a bundle of her hair and put the tip of my nose to it, to enjoy the scent.

rows.jp: 「一長一短なんだ。そのことをわかっておくれ、私の素敵な淑女よ」
rows.en: “Everything has its strengths and weaknesses. Try to understand that, my lovely lady.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You have shortcomings and strong points. This is what this one would like to have you understand, oh my fair lady."
ghs.assessment: Reversing the conventional English order strengths and weaknesses loses no Japanese meaning. The defect is stiff third-person self-reference and fluency.
ghs.remedy: Use natural self-reference.

highlights.text: Taichi: "You have shortcomings and strong points. This is what this one would like to have you understand, oh my fair lady."

rows.jp: 「よくわからないけど、わかったわ」
rows.en: “I don’t really get it, but I get it.”

ghs.en: Touko: "I don't really get it but, I get it, yes."
ghs.assessment: The source says that although she does not really understand, she accepts it. The final 'yes' adds an unsupported verbal tic.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I don't really understand, but all right.'

highlights.text: Touko: "I don't really get it but, I get it, yes."

rows.jp: 「……太一、恥ずかしいんだ。人前でベタベタするの」
rows.en: “…You’re embarrassed, aren’t you, Taichi? Being affectionate in public.”

ghs.en: Touko: "...Taichi, you're embarrassed. Of being all sticky-sticky in front of people that is."
ghs.assessment: The source is one inference that Taichi is embarrassed to be clingy in public. The English breaks the predicate into a sentence fragment beginning 'Of being.'
ghs.remedy: Use '...Taichi, you're embarrassed to be all clingy in public.'

highlights.text: Touko: "...Taichi, you're embarrassed. Of being all sticky-sticky in front of people that is."

rows.jp: あまりにもズレた理解に、お兄ちゃんの同義語にも聞こえかねない反問が、口をついて出る。
rows.en: Her conclusion was so far off that my ‘Huh?’ came out as ‘bruh’—as if I were calling her my big brother.

ghs.en: Her understanding shifted so far that even a flat English translation of onii-chan wasn't unlikely to slip my mouth in reply.
ghs.assessment: No macronized onii-chan is required. The real failures are untranslated address morphology, explanatory meta-commentary replacing the pun, and absence of a functioning English sound mechanism.
ghs.remedy: Create an English sound mechanism and localize the address.

highlights.text: Her understanding shifted so far that even a flat English translation of onii-chan wasn't unlikely to slip my mouth in reply.

ghs.en: Touko: "You have a cute side don't you."

rows.jp: ぺし、と背中を叩かれる。
rows.en: She gave my back a little pat.

ghs.en: Paf, I'm slapped on the back.

rows.en: Was she actually squeeing over me?

ghs.en: Have I just been thought moe?
ghs.assessment: 萌えられてる asks whether she is finding him endearingly moe. 'Thought moe' is not grammatical English and does not state her active response.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Does she find me cute?' or a consistently established rendering of moe.

highlights.text: Have I just been thought moe?

rows.jp: この醜形恐怖症でならした黒須太一ともあろうものが、萌えられているっ！？
rows.en: Taichi Kurosu, notorious for his body dysmorphia, had a girl squeeing over him?!

ghs.en: This chronically dysmorphophobic Kurosu Taichi here, of all people, thought moe?!
ghs.assessment: The boast identifies the narrator as someone renowned for dysmorphophobia and asks whether even he is being found cute. 'This chronically dysmorphophobic ... thought moe' is not a grammatical question.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Even Kurosu Taichi, renowned for his dysmorphophobia, is being found cute?!'

highlights.text: This chronically dysmorphophobic Kurosu Taichi here, of all people, thought moe?!

ghs.en: Should I let it go, should I?
ghs.assessment: The source asks once whether he can allow this. 'Should I let it go, should I?' duplicates the question as a malformed tag.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Can I allow this?'

highlights.text: Should I let it go, should I?

ghs.en: It was on the middle of the forehead.
ghs.assessment: The source specifies that the kiss landed on his forehead. 'The middle of' adds needless anatomical precision.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It was on my forehead.'

highlights.text: It was on the middle of the forehead.

rows.jp: 俺のトキメキ回路はショートした。

ghs.assessment: 笑う permits laugh or smile, and cherubic conveys innocent childlikeness. Only the noun fragment is defective.
ghs.remedy: Use a finite clause describing the cherubic smile or laugh.

highlights.text: Cherubic laughing.

rows.en: I hugged her before I knew it.

ghs.assessment: The source says he ended up hugging her. 'Totally' adds modern emphatic slang rather than the involuntary-result nuance of しまった.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I end up hugging her.'

highlights.text: I totally hugged her.

rows.en: Damn. She had caught me off guard.

ghs.assessment: 不覚を取った means he was caught off guard or suffered an embarrassing lapse. 'Complete defeat' turns it into the result of a contest.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Damn, she caught me off guard.'

highlights.text: Gah, that was complete defeat.

rows.jp: だがもう惑わされないぞ！
rows.en: But she wouldn’t fool me again!

ghs.en: But I shall never be fooled again!

rows.jp: そんなオノマトペごときでこの俺様がぁっ！
rows.en: As if a paltry onomatopoeia could move a man like me!

ghs.en: Not the Greatness that is I, not by that onomatopeiaaa!
ghs.assessment: The narrator protests that the great him cannot be overcome by mere onomatopoeia. 'Not the Greatness that is I, not by that onomatopeia' uses the wrong pronoun case, misspells 'onomatopoeia,' and does not state the action resisted.
ghs.remedy: Use 'As if mere onomatopoeia could overcome the great me!'

highlights.text: Not the Greatness that is I, not by that onomatopeiaaa!

rows.jp: 冬子が猫を真似て、胸元をひっかく。
rows.en: Touko played cat, scratching at my chest.

ghs.en: Imitating a cat, Touko scratches my belly.
ghs.assessment: 胸元 is the chest or breast area. 'Belly' moves the scratching to a different part of the body.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Imitating a cat, Tōko scratches at my chest.'

highlights.text: Imitating a cat, Touko scratches my belly.

rows.jp: バカップルここに爆誕。
rows.en: And with a bang, a lovey-dovey couple was born.

ghs.en:
A Syrupple has here
its explosive birth.
